# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260926-1607-apex-order-pickup-validation`
- Research system: `ChatGPT Deep Research`
- Started at: `2026-09-26 16:07 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-26 16:12 CDT`
- Research scope: Direct-competitor customer and product-page mining
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:apex-order-pickup`
- Methodology: Four first-party Apex Order Pickup customer, case-study, interview, or restaurant pages were opened and assessed. Vendor-authored results remain attributed claims and were not written into canonical records.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 0
- Conflicts found: 2
- Material takeaway: Apex has named deployment evidence across a Jersey Mike's campus location, Lehigh University dining, Santikos Entertainment, and OOMI Digital Kitchen. The strongest pages show Grubhub Campus integration, multi-bank campus expansion, and named Flow-Thru and AXCESS locker products, while corporate-system scope and current 2026 estate remain unproven.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Jersey Mike's at Rider University
- Vendor: Apex Order Pickup Solutions; Grubhub Campus
- Product or category: Automated pickup locker windows; mobile ordering integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: location-level
- Evidence type: testimonial interview
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Apex's first-party interview with a Grubhub Campus executive identifies Rider University and the Jersey Mike's location as an Apex example, while keeping the evidence scoped to that campus location.
- Source title: Grubhub Campus | Building Friendly, Fluid Experiences
- Source URL: https://apexorderpickup.com/building-friendly-fluid-experiences-on-campus/
- Publisher or source owner: Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Published date, if known: 2023-04-12
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The interview describes a Rider University Jersey Mike's renovated into a production-kitchen model that presents orders through locker windows, enabling throughput with a different front-of-house labor model.
- Product-specific evidence: Unattended locker-window pickup linked to campus mobile-ordering workflows; the page also describes Apex as a strategic locker partner to Grubhub Campus.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is a single campus location and does not establish a Jersey Mike's corporate deployment, a current chainwide relationship, or a named Apex hardware model.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm the Rider deployment's current status, specific Apex locker model, and whether any other Jersey Mike's locations use Apex.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Lehigh University Dining / The Grind
- Vendor: Apex Order Pickup Solutions; Grubhub Campus
- Product or category: Smart food lockers; QR-code pickup; Grubhub Campus integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Apex's dated first-party case study names Lehigh, a dining executive, the initial site, the Grubhub integration, measured pickup results, and subsequent campus expansion.
- Source title: 300% Sales Growth and a Whole Lot Less Chaos: How Lehigh University Transformed Pickup at The Grind
- Source URL: https://apexorderpickup.com/how-lehigh-university-transformed-pickup-at-the-grind/
- Publisher or source owner: Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Published date, if known: 2024-08-21
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Apex reports an initial locker bank at The Grind integrated with Grubhub Campus, followed by five additional locker banks at the Clayton University Center supporting multiple dining concepts.
- Product-specific evidence: Smart food lockers, Grubhub Campus ordering, QR-code compartment access, automated pickup notification, and six reported locker banks across the initial and later deployments.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page reports a 300% sales increase and 98% successful pickup rate but does not isolate locker causality or define the measurement window; the upcoming ghost-kitchen expansion was a plan, not a completed deployment.
- Recommended follow-up: Verify the reporting period, definition of successful pickup, and current count and placement of live locker banks.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Santikos Entertainment
- Vendor: Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Product or category: Flow-Thru 10,000 locker; AXCESS 2000.H heated pickup station
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Apex's first-party case-study PDF names Santikos executives, specific locker models, deployment counts, workflow, volume, and labor results.
- Source title: Movie Theater Eliminates Lines, Saves on Labor with Apex
- Source URL: https://apexorderpickup.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Apex-Santikos-Case-Study-min.pdf
- Publisher or source owner: Apex Supply Chain Technologies / Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Published date, if known: 2020
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Santikos selected Flow-Thru 10,000 and AXCESS 2000.H units, first deployed them at two locations, and added two more locations within months; the page reports more than 2,000 orders per week at each location and pickup labor falling from three employees to one.
- Product-specific evidence: Two-sided self-serve lockers and heated pickup stations, automatic guest notification, unique access code, scan-or-enter pickup, and configuration based on sales-transaction data.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The evidence is historical and covers four of a then-nine-location estate. Expansion beyond those sites and continued 2026 use are not established; performance figures are vendor-authored.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm Santikos' current estate, live Apex site count, and whether Flow-Thru and AXCESS models remain in service.

### Observation 4

- Brand: OOMI Digital Kitchen
- Vendor: Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Product or category: Smart food lockers
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: location-level
- Evidence type: customer video landing page
- Confidence: 75%
- Confidence rationale: Apex's current restaurant page explicitly names OOMI Digital Kitchen as using Apex smart lockers, but provides no location count, product model, deployment date, or named customer testimony in the page text.
- Source title: Smart Order Pickup for QSRs & Restaurants
- Source URL: https://apexorderpickup.com/qsrs-and-restaurants/
- Publisher or source owner: Apex Order Pickup Solutions
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The restaurant page says OOMI Digital Kitchen uses Apex smart lockers for fast, frictionless pickup and a simpler employee handoff workflow.
- Product-specific evidence: Apex smart food lockers for guest order handoff; the page does not identify a specific locker model or integration.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is promotional and scope-light. It does not support chainwide deployment, a particular site count, measured outcomes, or attribution of ApexIQ capabilities to OOMI.
- Recommended follow-up: Open or obtain a transcript of the linked customer video and verify deployment site, locker model, integrations, and current operating status.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: Apex's named customer pages establish current 2026 enterprise-wide deployments.
- Pages checked: All four pages in the source ledger.
- Result: Unsupported. Jersey Mike's is a single campus example, OOMI's scope is unspecified, Santikos is historical and partial, and Lehigh is campus-specific.
- Candidate or claim: Every result metric is attributable solely to Apex lockers.
- Pages checked: Lehigh and Santikos case studies.
- Result: Unsupported. The pages report outcomes but do not provide controlled attribution, complete measurement windows, or independent validation.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://apexorderpickup.com/building-friendly-fluid-experiences-on-campus/ | testimonial interview | 2026-09-26 | 1 | Productive; Jersey Mike's evidence is limited to the Rider University location. |
| https://apexorderpickup.com/how-lehigh-university-transformed-pickup-at-the-grind/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 2 | Productive; named Grubhub integration and multi-bank campus expansion. |
| https://apexorderpickup.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Apex-Santikos-Case-Study-min.pdf | case study | 2026-09-26 | 3 | Productive historical deployment with named hardware and four-site scope. |
| https://apexorderpickup.com/qsrs-and-restaurants/ | customer video landing page | 2026-09-26 | 4 | Productive but scope-light OOMI relationship; no named model or site count. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Apex's competitive strength is the handoff layer between digital ordering and physical fulfillment, with credible Grubhub Campus integration and workflow redesign evidence rather than a core POS offering.
- Inference: Apex can serve individual restaurant locations, multi-concept campus environments, and entertainment venues, but the reviewed pages do not establish a current national restaurant-chain estate.
